source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 4 (i)-(iii): area of a parallelogram from four vertices (opposite vertex found first) (book p.283). (iii) C printed without its minus sign. Answer key PDF 312.

blocks.prompt: 4 (i) Find the area of a parallelogram, whose vertices are: \(A(0, 0, 0)\), \(B(1, 2, 3)\), \(C(2, -1, 1)\), \(D(-1, 3, 2)\).
blocks.explanation:
An area question with four vertices.
We must find the area of the parallelogram.
Plan: find the vertex opposite to \(A\), take the two sides from \(A\), cross product, length.
steps:
Given: \(A(0, 0, 0)\), \(B(1, 2, 3)\), \(C(2, -1, 1)\), \(D(-1, 3, 2)\).
To find: the area of the parallelogram.
Method: Area \(= |\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|\) where \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}\) are two adjacent sides from one vertex (14.3.7 (a)). First we find which vertex is opposite to \(A\): the diagonals bisect each other, so opposite pairs have the same coordinate sum.

Find the vertex opposite to \(A\)
\[A + B = (1, 2, 3)\]
\[C + D = (1, 2, 3)\]
Why: The sums are equal, so \(A\) and \(B\) are opposite corners (both diagonals have the same midpoint). Going round, the vertices are \(A, C, B, D\); the sides from \(A\) go to \(C\) and \(D\).

Write the two adjacent sides
\[\underline{AC} = (2 - 0)\underline{i} + (-1 - 0)\underline{j} + (1 - 0)\underline{k}\]
\[= 2\underline{i} - \underline{j} + \underline{k}\]
\[\underline{AD} = (-1 - 0)\underline{i} + (3 - 0)\underline{j} + (2 - 0)\underline{k}\]
\[= -\underline{i} + 3\underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\]
Why: (end point) minus (starting point).

Write the determinant
\[\underline{AC} \times \underline{AD} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{AC}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{AD}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (-1)(2) - (1)(3) = -5\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (2)(2) - (1)(-1) = 5\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (2)(3) - (-1)(-1) = 5\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{AC} \times \underline{AD} = \underline{i}(-5) - \underline{j}(5) + \underline{k}(5)\]
\[= -5\underline{i} - 5\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Area = length of the cross product
\[|\underline{AC} \times \underline{AD}| = \sqrt{(-5)^2 + (-5)^2 + (5)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{75} = 5 \sqrt{3}\]
Why: \(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}| = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\) = base \(\times\) height.

Check with the diagonals
\[\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}\,|\underline{AB} \times \underline{CD}|\]
\[= 5\sqrt{3}\]
Why: The area of a parallelogram is also half the length of the cross product of its diagonals; it gives the same value.

blocks.prompt: 4 (ii) Find the area of a parallelogram, whose vertices are: \(A(1, 1, 1)\), \(B(4, 2, 3)\), \(C(5, 6, 7)\), \(D(2, 5, 5)\).
blocks.explanation:
An area question with four vertices.
We must find the area of the parallelogram.
Plan: find the vertex opposite to \(A\), take the two sides from \(A\), cross product, length.
steps:
Given: \(A(1, 1, 1)\), \(B(4, 2, 3)\), \(C(5, 6, 7)\), \(D(2, 5, 5)\).
To find: the area of the parallelogram.
Method: Area \(= |\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|\) where \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}\) are two adjacent sides from one vertex (14.3.7 (a)). First we find which vertex is opposite to \(A\): the diagonals bisect each other, so opposite pairs have the same coordinate sum.

Find the vertex opposite to \(A\)
\[A + C = (6, 7, 8)\]
\[B + D = (6, 7, 8)\]
Why: The sums are equal, so \(A\) and \(C\) are opposite corners (both diagonals have the same midpoint). Going round, the vertices are \(A, B, C, D\); the sides from \(A\) go to \(B\) and \(D\).

Write the two adjacent sides
\[\underline{AB} = (4 - 1)\underline{i} + (2 - 1)\underline{j} + (3 - 1)\underline{k}\]
\[= 3\underline{i} + \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{AD} = (2 - 1)\underline{i} + (5 - 1)\underline{j} + (5 - 1)\underline{k}\]
\[= \underline{i} + 4\underline{j} + 4\underline{k}\]
Why: (end point) minus (starting point).

Write the determinant
\[\underline{AB} \times \underline{AD} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 3 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & 4 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{AB}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{AD}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (1)(4) - (2)(4) = -4\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (3)(4) - (2)(1) = 10\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (3)(4) - (1)(1) = 11\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{AB} \times \underline{AD} = \underline{i}(-4) - \underline{j}(10) + \underline{k}(11)\]
\[= -4\underline{i} - 10\underline{j} + 11\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Area = length of the cross product
\[|\underline{AB} \times \underline{AD}| = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + (-10)^2 + (11)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{237}\]
Why: \(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}| = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\) = base \(\times\) height.

Check with the diagonals
\[\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}\,|\underline{AC} \times \underline{BD}|\]
\[= \sqrt{237}\]
Why: The area of a parallelogram is also half the length of the cross product of its diagonals; it gives the same value.

blocks.prompt: 4 (iii) Find the area of a parallelogram, whose vertices are: \(A(4, 5, 6)\), \(B(1, 3, 2)\), \(C(-2, 0, 1)\) [printed as \(C(\ 2, 0, 1)\)], \(D(1, 2, 5)\).
blocks.explanation:
An area question with four vertices.
We must find the area of the parallelogram.
Plan: find the vertex opposite to \(A\), take the two sides from \(A\), cross product, length.
steps:
Given: \(A(4, 5, 6)\), \(B(1, 3, 2)\), \(C(-2, 0, 1)\), \(D(1, 2, 5)\).
To find: the area of the parallelogram.
Method: Area \(= |\underline{u} \times \underline{v}|\) where \(\underline{u}, \underline{v}\) are two adjacent sides from one vertex (14.3.7 (a)). First we find which vertex is opposite to \(A\): the diagonals bisect each other, so opposite pairs have the same coordinate sum.

Find the vertex opposite to \(A\)
\[A + C = (2, 5, 7)\]
\[B + D = (2, 5, 7)\]
Why: The sums are equal, so \(A\) and \(C\) are opposite corners (both diagonals have the same midpoint). Going round, the vertices are \(A, B, C, D\); the sides from \(A\) go to \(B\) and \(D\).

Write the two adjacent sides
\[\underline{AB} = (1 - 4)\underline{i} + (3 - 5)\underline{j} + (2 - 6)\underline{k}\]
\[= -3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{AD} = (1 - 4)\underline{i} + (2 - 5)\underline{j} + (5 - 6)\underline{k}\]
\[= -3\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} - \underline{k}\]
Why: (end point) minus (starting point).

Write the determinant
\[\underline{AB} \times \underline{AD} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ -3 & -2 & -4 \\ -3 & -3 & -1 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{AB}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{AD}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (-2)(-1) - (-4)(-3) = -10\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (-3)(-1) - (-4)(-3) = -9\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (-3)(-3) - (-2)(-3) = 3\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{AB} \times \underline{AD} = \underline{i}(-10) - \underline{j}(-9) + \underline{k}(3)\]
\[= -10\underline{i} + 9\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Area = length of the cross product
\[|\underline{AB} \times \underline{AD}| = \sqrt{(-10)^2 + (9)^2 + (3)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{190}\]
Why: \(|\underline{u} \times \underline{v}| = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\sin\theta\) = base \(\times\) height.

Check with the diagonals
\[\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}\,|\underline{AC} \times \underline{BD}|\]
\[= \sqrt{190}\]
Why: The area of a parallelogram is also half the length of the cross product of its diagonals; it gives the same value.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the third vertex as \(C(\ 2, 0, 1)\) with the sign of the first coordinate missing. With \(C(2, 0, 1)\) the four points do not form a parallelogram (no pair of vertices has the same coordinate sum as the other pair). The intended vertex is \(C(-2, 0, 1)\): then \(A + C = B + D = (2, 5, 7)\) and the area is \(\sqrt{190}\), the answer in the key.
